correctness.rationale: The definitions of popularity and lexicographic rank maximality are applied to the same perfect-matching set. Independent exhaustive reconstruction in this audit reproduced the complete three-agent census: 138 profiles with equality of the rank-maximal and popular sets, 72 with the rank-maximal set a proper subset of the popular set, and 6 profiles with no popular matching, exactly the six identical-order profiles. The displayed four-agent witness was also checked from the actual package code: its best rank signature is \((2,1,1,0)\), it has four rank-maximal matchings and exactly two popular matchings, with the latter a proper subset. The package verifier additionally compares direct majority voting against the Abraham--Irving--Kavitha--Mehlhorn characterization and two independent rank-maximal encodings.

value.rationale: Rank maximality and popularity are two standard, competing optimality notions in one-sided allocation. Locating their first possible conflict and completely resolving every smaller market gives a natural finite cutoff with a reproducible exact census, not an arbitrary slice.

final_claim: In balanced complete one-sided house-allocation markets with strict preferences, every three-agent instance that admits a popular matching has every rank-maximal matching popular, while four agents already admit an instance with popular matchings but with some rank-maximal matchings nonpopular; the complete two- and three-agent census and the displayed four-agent witness are exact.
limitations: Balanced complete strict one-sided preferences only.
The theorem is a sharp small-market boundary and census, not a structural classification for arbitrary market size.
